327325.title: The $\gamma_3$ period conjecture for rider pieces
327325.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbf{M}$ be the move set of a piece $\mathbb P$, with basic moves $(c_r,d_r)$, and write

$$
\hat d_r:=\max(|c_r|,|d_r|),\qquad \Lambda:=\operatorname{lcm}\{\hat d_r:m_r\in\mathbf{M}\}.
$$

Let $\gamma_3$ denote the third coefficient of the quasipolynomial $u_{\mathbb P}(q;n)$. **The $\gamma_3$ period conjecture.** The period of $\gamma_3$ is either $1$ or $\Lambda$.

The claim is supported in the paper by several examples, including two pieces, arbitrary numbers of one-move riders, three partial queens, and two partial nightriders, but no general proof is given.

327365.title: The divisibility conjecture for truncated northeast triangular posets
327365.literal_statement:
Let $\operatorname*{NEtri}(p)$ be the northeast triangular poset, let $s\in\mathbb{N}$, and define the subposet

$$
\operatorname*{NEtri}\nolimits^{\prime}(p)=\left\{(i,k)\in\operatorname*{NEtri}(p)\mid k\geq s\right\}.
$$

Let $R_{\operatorname*{NEtri}\nolimits^{\prime}(p)}$ denote birational rowmotion on this subposet, and write $\operatorname*{ord}(R)$ for the order of a birational map. **The truncated northeast triangular divisibility conjecture.** For every integer $p>1$ and every $s\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
\operatorname*{ord}\left(R_{\operatorname*{NEtri}\nolimits^{\prime}(p)}\right)\mid p.
$$

This is presented as a generalization suggested by Nathan Williams of the northeast triangular order conjecture. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution.

327713.title: Manoussakis's pancyclicity conjecture for digraphs
327713.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a strongly connected digraph on $n$ vertices. For vertices $x,y,z\in V(D)$, say that $x$ is **nonadjacent** to $y$ when neither arc between them is present. A digraph is **pancyclic** if it contains directed cycles of every length allowed by the conjecture.

**Manoussakis's conjecture.** If, for every triple $x,y,z\in V(D)$ with $x$ nonadjacent to $y$, the inequalities

$$
d(x)+d(y)+d^+(x)+d^-(z)\geq 3n+1
$$

when $xz\notin A(D)$, and

$$
d(x)+d(y)+d^+(z)+d^-(x)\geq 3n+1
$$

when $zx\notin A(D)$, hold, then $D$ is pancyclic.

This is a proposed pancyclic analogue of Manoussakis-type Hamiltonicity degree conditions. The supplied source does not report a resolution.

327844.title: Primitivity conjecture for groups generated by a supersimple design
327844.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal{D}=(\Omega,\mathcal{B})$ be a supersimple $2$-$(n,4,\lambda)$ design, and let $\pi_\infty(\mathcal{D})$ denote the group associated with the point $\infty\in\Omega$. **Primitivity conjecture.** For all $\lambda>0$, there exists $f(\lambda)$ such that either $\pi_\infty(\mathcal{D})$ acts primitively on $\Omega\setminus\{\infty\}$ or $n<f(\lambda)$. This conjecture would imply that the associated permutation group is eventually the full symmetric or alternating group, according to the parity of $\lambda$, but the conjecture itself remains open.

328246.title: The upper matching conjecture for regular graphs
328246.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph on $2n$ vertices, with $d\mid 2n$, and let ${\mathcal M}(G)$ be its collection of all matchings. Write $K(n,d)$ for the disjoint union of $n/d$ copies of $K_{d,d}$. **Upper matching conjecture.** If $G$ is bipartite, or if $G$ is arbitrary, then

$$
|{\mathcal M}(G)|\leq|{\mathcal M}(K(n,d))|.
$$

The question extends the known extremal inequality for perfect matchings; the source identifies the bipartite case as the heart of the matter and explains that it would imply the general case.

328247.title: The upper matching conjecture for matchings of each size
328247.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph on $2n$ vertices, with $d\mid 2n$, and let ${\mathcal M}_t(G)$ denote its matchings of size $t$. Write $K(n,d)$ for the disjoint union of $n/d$ copies of $K_{d,d}$. **Upper matching conjecture.** If $G$ is bipartite, or if $G$ is arbitrary, then for every $0\leq t\leq n$,

$$
|{\mathcal M}_t(G)|\leq|{\mathcal M}_t(K(n,d))|.
$$

This is the stronger coefficientwise form of the conjecture that the total number of matchings is maximized by the disjoint union of complete bipartite graphs.

328249.title: The Widom–Rowlinson extremal conjecture for regular graphs
328249.literal_statement:
Let $H_{\rm WR}$ be the complete fully looped graph on three vertices with one non-loop edge removed, equivalently the complete looped path on three vertices. Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex, $d$-regular graph, and let ${\rm hom}(G,H_{\rm WR})$ denote the number of homomorphisms from $G$ to $H_{\rm WR}$. **Widom–Rowlinson conjecture.** For every $n$ and $d$,

$$
{\rm hom}(G,H_{\rm WR})\leq {\rm hom}(K_{d+1},H_{\rm WR})^{n/(d+1)}.
$$

Homomorphisms to $H_{\rm WR}$ encode configurations in the Widom–Rowlinson model. The source describes the conjecture as a target for an entropy proof and records only a related weak result for a larger family of graphs.

328378.title: The maximal affine-set direction conjecture
328378.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}\subseteq\operatorname{AG}(2,q)$ be a maximal affine set, let $\mathcal{D}$ be the set of directions determined by $\mathcal{U}$, and let $s(y)$ and $t(y)$ denote the associated parameters for each $y\in\mathcal{D}$.

**Maximal affine-set direction conjecture.** If $\mathcal{U}$ is maximal, then

$$
t(y)=s(y)
$$

for all $y\in\mathcal{D}$ such that $t(y)>2$.

The conjecture is motivated by polynomial completing results and the fact that a maximal affine set cannot be completed without determining additional directions. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

328555.title: Image maximality conjecture for the DH-matrix
328555.literal_statement:
Let ${\bf D}$ be the DH-matrix, and say that a matrix is **image maximal** when it is not properly image dominated by any image partition regular extension. The preceding theorem states that every image partition regular matrix obtained from ${\bf D}$ by adjoining finitely many rows is image dominated by ${\bf D}$.

**Image maximality conjecture.** The system ${\bf D}$ is image maximal.

The theorem establishes only finite image maximality: every finite-row image partition regular extension is image dominated by ${\bf D}$. The conjecture strengthens this to image maximality without the finite-extension restriction; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

328739.title: The infinite-group partition conjecture for covering numbers
328739.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an infinite group of cardinality $\varkappa$. For a subset $A\subseteq G$, define

$$
\operatorname{cov}(A)=\min\{|X|:X\subseteq G,\ G=XA\}.
$$

**Partition conjecture.** The group $G$ can be partitioned into countably many subsets

$$
G=\bigcup_{n<\omega}A_n
$$

such that

$$
\operatorname{cov}(A_nA_n^{-1})=\varkappa
$$

for every $n<\omega$. This conjecture strengthens the preceding question about partitions into fewer than $|G|$ cells and asks for uniformly maximal covering numbers of the difference sets of all cells; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

328889.title: The inverse sieve conjecture in rough form
328889.literal_statement: Let $X\subset [N]$ be a subset. Suppose that, for every prime $p$, the reduction $X\pmod p$ occupies at most $0.9p$ residue classes. **Inverse sieve conjecture, rough form.** Either $X$ has extremely small cardinality, or $X$ possesses algebraic structure. This informal formulation motivates more precise finitary and infinitary versions; the precise meaning of “extremely small” and “algebraic structure” is not specified here.

328989.title: The fractional clique-cover conjecture for triangle-free graphs
328989.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an undirected triangle-free graph. The **fractional clique-cover conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{gn}(G)=|V(G)|-\kappa_f(G).
$$

The fractional clique cover gives a general lower bound on the guessing number, and equality is known for several graph families. The corresponding equality for arbitrary undirected graphs was disproved by Baber, while the triangle-free case is posed here as a natural restricted question.

329130.title: Functional-equation formulation of the Riemann hypothesis for graph spectral zeta functions
329130.literal_statement:
Let $h_n(s)$ be defined by

$$
h_n(s)=(4\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(s/2)n^{-s}\left(\zeta_{\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}}(s/2)-n\zeta_{\mathbb{Z}}(s/2)\right).
$$

**Functional-equation conjecture.** For every $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with $0<\operatorname{Re}(s)<1$,

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\left|\frac{h_n(1-s)}{h_n(s)}\right|=1.
$$

This is presented as a formulation of the Riemann hypothesis in terms of the functional behavior of spectral zeta functions of graphs, and as heuristic evidence for the validity of the Riemann hypothesis. The source does not state a resolution of this conjecture.

329173.title: Polynomial singularity bound conjecture for random regular digraphs
329173.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a uniform random element of the set of $n\times n$ zero-one matrices with every row and column sum equal to $d$. **Polynomial singularity conjecture.** There are absolute constants $C,c>0$ such that, for every $3\leq d\leq n-3$,

$$
\pr\big(\det(M)=0\big)\leq Cn^{-c}.
$$

The conjecture extends the paper's polynomial singularity estimate to all nontrivial degrees in the stated range. It is presented as an open conjecture in the supplied text.

329224.title: The Janson–Sós conjecture on quasi-random properties from graph averages
329224.literal_statement:
Let $F \neq K_2$ be a non-empty graph with vertex set $\{1,\ldots,m\}$, and let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m \in (0,1)$ satisfy

$$
\sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i \leqslant 1.
$$

Write $\mathcal{P}(F,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)$ for the property defined by the corresponding average over products of disjoint vertex sets, and let $p \in (0,1]$. **Janson–Sós conjecture.** The property $\mathcal{P}(F,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)$ is a quasi-random property for every $p \in (0,1]$. This addresses the problem of determining when these properties are always quasi-random; before this work it was unknown even for the path on three vertices and was stated as an open problem by Janson and Sós. The exceptional known non-example is $\mathcal{P}(K_2,\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})$; the claim excludes it.

329273.title: Alon–Shpilka–Umans' sunflower conjecture over ${\mathbb Z}_D^n$
329273.literal_statement:
Let ${\mathbb Z}_D=\{1,\ldots,D\}$. Vectors $v_1,v_2,v_3\in{\mathbb Z}_D^n$ form a **$3$-sunflower** if, in every coordinate, their entries are either all equal or all distinct. **Alon–Shpilka–Umans' sunflower conjecture.** There exist $\varepsilon>0$, $D_0$, and $n_0$ such that for every $D\geq D_0$ and $n\geq n_0$, every collection ${\cal F}$ of vectors in ${\mathbb Z}_D^n$ with

$$
|{\cal F}|\geq D^{(1-\varepsilon)n}
$$

contains a $3$-sunflower. This is an equivalent vector formulation of the Boolean-cube sunflower conjecture and is widely believed to be true, but remains open.

329274.title: Alon–Shpilka–Umans' weak sunflower conjecture over ${\mathbb Z}_D$
329274.literal_statement:
Let ${\mathbb Z}_D=\{1,\ldots,D\}$, and call three vectors in ${\mathbb Z}_D^n$ a **$3$-sunflower** when their entries in each coordinate are either all equal or all distinct. **Alon–Shpilka–Umans' weak sunflower conjecture.** For the fixed integer $D$ considered here, there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and $n_0$ such that for every $n\geq n_0$, every collection ${\cal F}$ of vectors in ${\mathbb Z}_D^n$ with

$$
|{\cal F}|\geq D^{(1-\varepsilon)n}
$$

contains a $3$-sunflower. This is the fixed-$D$ variant of the preceding sunflower conjecture and is presented as a question about whether the assertion holds for small $D$.

329466.title: Perrot–Pham sink-independence conjecture for the Biggs–Merino polynomial
329466.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a strongly connected digraph, and let $s$ be a sink vertex. For the set of $s$-recurrent configurations modulo the relation $\stackrel{s}{\sim}$, define the Biggs–Merino polynomial by

$$
\mathcal B(G,s;y):=\sum_{[\widehat{\mathbf{c}}]\in\operatorname{Rec}(G,\stackrel{s}{\sim})}y^{\operatorname{dlvl}([\widehat{\mathbf{c}}])}.
$$

**Perrot–Pham's conjecture.** The polynomial $\mathcal B(G,s;y)$ is independent of the choice of the sink vertex $s$.

Perrot and Pham proved this independence for connected Eulerian digraphs and conjectured it for all strongly connected digraphs. The paper states that its main theorem answers this conjecture, so the conjecture is solved.

329527.title: Positivity conjecture for structure coefficients of the matroid Kazhdan–Lusztig basis
329527.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid with lattice of flats $L(M)$, let $E_q(M)$ be its $q$-deformed Möbius algebra, and let $\{x_F\mid F\in L(M)\}$ be the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis. Define structure coefficients $C_{FG}^H(q)\in\mathbb{Z}[q]$ by

$$
x_F\cdot x_G=\sum_H C_{FG}^H(q)x_H.
$$

**Structure-coefficient positivity conjecture.** For all $F,G,H\in L(M)$, $C_{FG}^H(q)\in\mathbb{N}[q]$. The conjecture was disproved by examples in rank $4$ and higher, including a uniform matroid of rank $4$ on $6$ elements.

331918.title: Ben Efraim's lexicographic edge-isoperimetric conjecture for the transposition graph
331918.literal_statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, and let $T_n$ be its transposition graph. For $\mathcal{A} \subset S_n$, write $\partial \mathcal{A}$ for its edge-boundary in $T_n$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the initial segment of the lexicographic order on $S_n$ having size $|\mathcal{A}|$. **Ben Efraim's conjecture.** For every $\mathcal{A} \subset S_n$, 

$$
|\partial \mathcal{A}| \geq |\partial \mathcal{C}|.
$$

This would give an edge-isoperimetric inequality for the transposition graph that is sharp for every set size; the source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
